description: Found 2026-11-15 (bitstring split experiments, /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-bitstring-split.html section 8a). On fz-nml.11 31823421d: 'defmodule Main do def build(n), do: <<1::size(n)>> end' and 'fn n -> <<1::size(n)>> end' both emit warning[lower/unused-variable] for n, though n is read as the segment size; '{n, <<1::size(n)>>}' does not warn. Warnings are errors under our rules, so a correct Elixir program fails to compile cleanly. Elixir does not warn. Introduced with fz-rik (unused-variable warning): the use collector does not visit a bitstring segment's size expression in construction. Acceptance: fixture with size(n) in a def body, a fn body and a match pattern (size(n) after n is bound) produces no warning on interp/run/build; an actually unused variable beside it still warns.

comments.text: Another form, found by the fz-nml.8 builder (JSON session, develop 4a05ae2be): `def g(x, s), do: <<x :: float-size(s)>>` warns unused-variable "s" though s is read as the size and the output is correct. The acceptance fixture should cover a size inside a typed segment (float-size(s)) as well as size(n).
Owner: Binary Handling. PR #781 (one-arm scope-walk fix + fixture 01821, oracle self). Blocks fz-9e2.3's fixture.

title: A variable used only as a segment size is not reported unused
